Note (1): Pipelines are as follows:
    COR = Envelope autocorrelation function (EACF), as described in
        Mosser & Appourchaux (2009) [2009A&A...508..877M];
    ELS = Methods described in Elsworth et al. (2020) [2020RNAAS...4..177E];
    GAU = Designed to estimate {nu}max, {Delta}{nu}, and Amax, the
        amplitude of the Gaussian function employed to model the
        oscillations' power excess;
    SYD = SYD pipeline, Huber et al. (2009) [2009CoAst.160...74H];
    A2Z = Combination of the A2Z (Mathur et al. 2010
        [2010A&A...511A..46M]) and an implementation of the EACF
         (COR) method;
    DIA = Adoption of the Bayesian inference code DIAMONDS, Corsaro &
        De Ridder (2014) [2014A&A...571A..71C];
    CAN = Described in APOKASC-2 paper, Pinsonneault et al. (2018)
        [2018ApJS..239...32P] and in Kallinger et al. (2010) 
        [2010A&A...522A...1K];
    CV  = "Coefficient of Variation" (CV) method for detecting
        solar-like oscillations and reporting νmax values is
        described in Bell et al. (2019) [2019MNRAS.482..616B];
    HON = Deep learning to detect the presence of a power excess
        corresponding to solar-like oscillations within power
        spectra. As described in Hon et al. (2018) [2018ApJ...859...64H];
    FLI = FliPer method described in Bugnet et al. (2018)
        [2018A&A...620A..38B] is based on the averaged power density
        contained in the PSD.
Note (2): Flags, which reflect the category of the data ({nu}max or
    {Delta}{nu}) for each star are as follows:
    0 = no data;
    1 = valid filtered measurement;
    2 = failed the spectroscopic prior;
    6 = failed the ensemble prior test;
    9 = data excluded from usage because it fell outside the range of 
        validity for that pipeline.
